approved: Marriage Equality Amendment Bill 2013 - Second Reading - Speed things along

A motion was moved to introduce the Marriage Equality Amendment Bill 2013, which would amend the Marriage Act 1961 to allow marriage equality regardless of sex, sexual orientation, or gender identity. The motion was agreed to and the bill was read a first time.

The Marriage Equality Amendment Bill 2013 seeks to redefine marriage as between two people regardless of sex, sexual orientation or gender identity. The speaker noted that 62% of Australians support same-sex marriage, called on parliamentarians to co-sponsor the bill, and referenced the High Court's overturning of ACT marriage laws.
